newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland says no plans to revalue gold reserves.
newsitem.headline: Ireland says no plans to revalue gold reserves.

text.p: Ireland's central bank said on Friday it had no plans to revalue its gold reserves.
"We have no plans to revalue the gold reserves...we have a very small proportion of our reserves in gold so the issue is not of any major significance to us," a spokesman for the central bank said.
The central bank said its most recent statistics -- from March -- showed gold accounted for 80 million Irish pounds ($122.6 million), or 1.3 percent, of 6.0 billion pounds of total reserves.
The spokesman said the central bank had always valued its gold reserves at the current market value.
German finance minister Theo Waigel has proposed revaluing the Bundesbank's gold reserves to help Germany tighten its finances and allow the country to take part in the European single currency.
